before.label: Gender & racial formation
before.description: Examines how gender and race are historically produced through relations of power. Intersectional approaches question treating race, class, and gender separately. Some feminist and gender historians built on British Marxist social history’s attention to labour, culture, and agency while reworking its concepts and questioning gendered exclusions. These exchanges do not define every strand of gender or racial-formation analysis.

after.label: Gender history
after.description: Examines gender as a historically changing organization of social relations, identities and power. Research on work, family, masculinity, bodies and colonial settings connects gender to class, race and other relations without reducing these to one framework. Some feminist historians develop and criticize British Marxist social history; this is one route among several.
